label: late copy-phase steps (recall_idx >= 6) with input among d/z/2/u/s/f/p/b/n/w
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original or delimiter steps), and only late in long sequences: zero below t=8, and the rate climbs steeply with t and recall_idx (19.5% at t=17). 71% of mass comes from L=9, and it concentrates on the last few outputs (to_go 0-2 hold ~89% of mass). Within those late steps it prefers particular input tokens (d, z, 2, u most, then s, f, p, b, n, w; t and q almost never) and, more weakly, particular output tokens (2, p, 3, t, k). It also rises with the number of digits in the sequence. Never fires on a first occurrence of a token. Late step, preferred input token and preferred output token look like additive evidence pushing it over the threshold: t=17 with input in {d,z,2,u} and output in {2,p,3} is 93% precise but rare. So the boolean predicate catches most of the mass but has low precision (~0.27): many late steps with preferred inputs stay below threshold. Magnitude is largest at the final steps of L=9 sequences.
